text: By midmorning on Tuesday, the refrigerators at Lindqvist Dairy’s small dispatch hall in Westmere were humming around a single notice: a voluntary recall of its oat yoghurt line after routine quality testing flagged an off-flavour linked to a packaging fault. The company said the issue affects 6,400 cups sold across Northfold and neighboring districts between 4 and 9 November, with batch codes 11A and 11B. No illnesses have been reported. Founded in 1987 as a butter cooperative, Lindqvist shifted into plant-based foods five years ago, riding a regional taste for lighter, dairy-free staples. In a brief statement, managing director Sanna Vek said customers could return unopened tubs to stores for a refund, while the rest of the week’s production was halted pending review.
